events.title: Autumn Days at Filoli
events.why: Seasonal daytime version with a hay maze, pumpkin meadow and the Autumn Railway, daily through Nov 1.

events.title: Corte Madera Oktoberfest
events.why: Small-town Marin Oktoberfest in a park, listed in Marin Mommies' fall fairs roundup as family-friendly.

events.title: Day of the Horse: Family Horse Fair
events.why: Woodside's annual equestrian celebration next door to Menlo Park, with a family horse fair on Sunday themed Year of the Fire Horse (a progressive trail ride for riders is on Saturday Oct 10).

events.title: Healdsburg Crush Wine Tasting (adults only)
events.why: Adults-only: 60+ Sonoma wine producers pouring at one harvest-season tasting that benefits the Boys & Girls Clubs.

events.title: San Francisco Italian Heritage Parade
events.venue: Fisherman's Wharf to Washington Square via Columbus Ave
events.why: One of the oldest Italian heritage parades in the US, with floats, marching bands and the Concorso Italiano car show in North Beach.

events.title: Shared Sky Festival (Day 2)
events.why: One-weekend festival bringing together Bay Area astronomy, art and photography communities at the hilltop observatory.

events.title: Welcome Back Monarch Butterfly Festival
events.why: Annual welcome for the returning monarchs at California's only monarch-preserve state park, with a parade, music, pumpkin ice cream and a talk by Julia Butterfly Hill ($10 parking).

events.title: Woodside Day of the Horse: Family Horse Fair
events.why: Once-a-year horse-town fair 15 minutes from Menlo Park with pony rides, a blacksmith demo, equine crafts and a chance to win a riding lesson.

events.title: 53rd Safeway World Championship Pumpkin Weigh-Off
events.why: Forklifts hoist one-ton-plus pumpkins onto the scale as growers chase a $30,000 world-record prize, a quirky local tradition that falls on the Indigenous Peoples' Day school holiday.

events.title: Alcatraz Sunrise Gathering for Indigenous Peoples' Day
events.why: Dawn ceremony on Alcatraz commemorating the 1969 occupation, with Native dancers and speakers; a once-a-year experience that requires an early ferry.

events.title: Safeway World Championship Pumpkin Weigh-Off
events.why: 53rd annual weigh-off on the Monday holiday where growers haul in pumpkins over a ton chasing $9 a pound and a $30,000 world-record bonus.

events.title: Sunrise Gathering on Alcatraz for Indigenous Peoples' Day
events.why: A memorable pre-dawn ferry to a sunrise ceremony commemorating the 1969-71 occupation of Alcatraz, a meaningful school-holiday outing for older kids.

events.title: Tween Hangout: Haunted Gingerbread Houses
events.why: Library program aimed precisely at ages 9 to 13: build spooky gingerbread houses on a weekday afternoon.

events.title: Nightfall at Filoli
events.why: After-dark walk through 1,000 jack-o'-lanterns, troll sculptures and a haunted railway on the estate gardens; runs nightly through Nov 1, last entry 8:30pm.

events.title: The Addams Family (San Marin High School musical)
events.why: Student production of the Halloween-season musical; also Oct 15 and 17 at 7pm and a 2pm matinee Oct 18.

events.title: 51st Potrero Hill R&B Festival
events.why: Four-block neighborhood street festival with two music stages, run as a fundraiser for local schools and the Potrero Hill Neighborhood House.

events.title: Bay Area Science Festival
events.why: Free one-day STEM fair with 125+ hands-on exhibits from local labs and companies, ideal for curious 9 to 14 year olds.

events.title: Bearrison Street Fair (adult-oriented)
events.why: Adults-only: a SoMa street fair celebrating the LGBTQ bear community with music, vendors and beer; not for kids.

events.title: Boo at the Zoo
events.why: Opening weekend of the zoo's Halloween run: House of Bugs encounters at 1pm Saturdays, reptile discoveries Sundays, trading-card hunt and a noon costume contest; included with regular admission.

events.title: Campbell Oktoberfest
events.why: 31st annual South Bay Oktoberfest with 125 booths, five stages and a kids' zone; continues Sunday Oct 18 until 5pm.

events.title: Filipino American International Book Festival
events.venue: San Francisco Main Library, 100 Larkin St
events.why: Largest Filipino American literary festival in the US, with author panels on comics, horror and mythology plus a marketplace, during Filipino American History Month.

events.title: Half Moon Bay Art & Pumpkin Festival
events.why: The coast's signature once-a-year festival: 275 artists, giant pumpkin carving, the Great Pumpkin Parade at noon Saturday, and everything pumpkin; continues Sunday Oct 18.

events.title: Shipyard Open Studios, Fall 2026
events.why: Twice-a-year chance to walk into 130+ working artist studios on the old naval shipyard, with kids' art activities, live jazz and a beer garden; free with RSVP, also Sunday Oct 18.

events.title: Spooky Times at Deer Hollow Farm
events.venue: Deer Hollow Farm, Rancho San Antonio Open Space Preserve
events.why: Annual haunted barnyard and Halloween games at a working farm in the preserve, $7 if you come in costume; last entry 2:30pm.

events.title: Thomas and Percy's Halloween Party at Roaring Camp
events.why: Ride a real steam train through the redwoods behind Thomas and Percy with Halloween activities; hourly departures 10am to 3pm, also Oct 18, 24 and 25.

events.title: Twilight Nature Walk at the Baylands
events.why: Free guided dusk walk to watch bats and evening birds in the Baylands, ages 6+, registration required.

events.title: UNAFF & Kids Program (United Nations Association Film Festival)
events.why: Free youth documentary session inside the 29th UNAFF, a Palo Alto-born human-rights film festival running Oct 15 to 25 at Mitchell Park Community Center and other venues; other sessions are $19 and free for students.

events.title: Harding Carnival & Pumpkin Patch
events.venue: Harding Park and Clubhouse, 7115 C Street
events.why: Elementary school PTA carnival with games, live music and magic, food and a pumpkin patch; a true neighborhood event tourists never see.

events.title: Palo Alto Art Center Fall Family Day
events.venue: Palo Alto Art Center, 1313 Newell Rd
events.why: Free afternoon of foil monoprints, collage and foam printing, plus a new Teen Zone with button and jewelry making and board games aimed at older kids.

events.title: Sunday Streets Excelsior
events.venue: Silver Ave and Geneva Ave corridor
events.why: Car-free street party where kids can bike and skate the Excelsior's main drag, with free activities and performances.
